# Captions

## Words and timings

- `npx hyperframes transcribe <file> --json` and a HeyGen voiceover (`/media-use`) give every word's start and end. Work from those as `[{ "id": "w0", "text": "Hello", "start": 0.0, "end": 0.5 }, …]`.
- `npx hyperframes transcribe` defaults to the `small.en` whisper model, which **translates** non-English speech into English. Pass the model: `npx hyperframes transcribe <file> --model small.en` for English, `--model small --language <code>` otherwise, `--model medium.en` for speech over music. It writes `assets/transcript.json` (its JSON names the path) and overwrites it on the next run; `--to srt` or `--to vtt` writes a sidecar.
- For Chinese, Japanese and other unspaced scripts, local transcription returns a whole sentence as one "word", sometimes in the other script (Traditional for Simplified speech). Split each segment's text into short phrases and spread its time across them by character count; check the characters against what is said.
- Whisper invents "Thank you." over silence and repeats lines over a silent tail: drop words that start inside a final silence (`silencedetect=noise=-35dB:d=0.6`; real speech sits around −16 to −26 dB).
- Never put two words in one timed entry, and match transcript words to caption words by position, not text, or a repeated word takes the wrong time.
- Read the transcript before using it. More than 20% `♪` or `�` tokens, or nonsense words, means it failed: retry with a larger model, or take lyrics from the person. Drop non-word tokens before building groups.

## Structure

- One sub-composition host with `data-track-kind="captions"` holds every caption group, so Studio shows them on one captions track.
- Ready-made styles: `npx hyperframes catalog --tag caption-style --json`. An installed one is source you can restyle.

## Groups

- 2–3 words for high energy, 3–5 conversational, 4–6 calm. Break at a sentence end, a pause of 150 ms or more, or the word limit.
- One group visible at a time. A group opens at or before its first word's start and closes at or after its last word's end. A caption at exactly 0 s looks pre-existing: start 0.1–0.3 s in.
- Every group ends with a hard kill after its exit, or a stale group can stay on screen:

```js
tl.to(group, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.12, ease: "power2.in" }, end - 0.12);
tl.set(group, { opacity: 0, visibility: "hidden" }, end);
```

`tl.set` is an instant flip, so setting `visibility` on the group is fine; never tween it on a `.clip`.

## Fit and place

- Size each group to fit: `window.__hyperframes.fitTextFontSize(text, { fontFamily, fontWeight, maxWidth })` returns `{ fontSize }`. Defaults: `maxWidth` 1600 landscape, 900 portrait; base 78, minimum 42, step 2. When a word scales up for emphasis, divide `maxWidth` by that scale.
- A full-width absolute container, centred with text alignment. Never `left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)`, which clips at the frame edges.
- `overflow: visible`, not `hidden`, which cuts off scaled words and glows.
- Landscape: 80–120 px from the bottom. Portrait: about 600–700 px from the bottom. Never over the speaker's face; inside the 80% title-safe box.
- Position each group absolutely. In a flex column a group hidden with `visibility: hidden` still takes space, so the next one lands lower. In a stack that accumulates, groups in one block share one exit time, or the stack reflows.
- Fade the group or its words, not both: the opacities multiply and read as a pop. A gradient or `background-clip: text` fill goes on the inner text span, not the transformed container.
- Over footage, choose the blend by the brightness (0–255) behind the text: under 60 `screen`, 60–180 `overlay`, over 180 `normal` with opaque colour. Plain subtitles above brightness 60 get a scrim sized to the text (30–40%), never a full-width bar.
- Footage may already carry burned-in subtitles only mid-clip: scan a 1 fps contact sheet before placing captions.

## Text behind the speaker

- Stack the video, then the captions, then a cutout of the person from `npx hyperframes remove-background` (`/media-use`), ordered by `z-index`. Shake or punch in the video and the cutout together in one wrapper.
- `check` treats a `<video>` as opaque across its whole box, so a WebM cutout fails every caption behind it with `text_occluded`: put `data-layout-allow-occlusion` on the cutout and judge from `snapshot`.
- A big word behind the head reads best 30–55% covered: under about 15% it floats, over about 65% it is eaten. Re-lay out when a content word is 80% covered, or two adjacent words 50% each. Measure the rendered word boxes against the matte over each caption's own time window (heads move: one clip went from y=224 to y=96 in 8 s); estimates from character widths were wrong both ways.
- The matte model drops mic arms, lets large rigs near the body leak in, and flickers on held objects. Its first run downloads 168 MB, and it runs at about 2 fps at 1080p on CPU.

# Films from a source: measured facts

What is specific to HyperFrames, or was measured on shipped films, when one video is made from a website, a script, a pull request, a music track, a real place or a short motion brief. The story comes first, from `story.md`; the shape of each kind of film is in `types/`. Motion craft is in `motion.md`, look in `look.md`, sound in `sound.md`, captions in `captions.md`.

## Script and pacing

- TTS reads about 2.2 words a second. Keep a scene to about 19 words (9 s); at most two scenes may reach 26 words (12 s). 30–90 s is about 155 words or fewer; a whole film about 400 at most.
- A voiceover longer than its visuals makes the visuals pad with idle drift. Trim the script; never stretch the motion.
- Everything on screen in the first quarter of a scene, then frozen, reads as a slideshow. Reveal each piece when the voiceover names it, across the back half of the scene; write the voiceover as separate phrases so it has cue points.
- Up to about six short scenes, build them yourself in one context (about 9 min for five, against about 21 min split across sub-agents). Beyond that, give each worker two or three scenes and start them all at once; a second wave nearly doubles the time.

## From a website

- `npx hyperframes capture <url> --json` writes `screenshots/full-page.png`: a 1x plate of the whole page, taken after the scroll pass with sticky and fixed elements made static, pixel-exact for a 1920-wide viewport travelling down it. It is skipped above 16384 px tall (use `scroll-*.png`); pushing in past 1:1 needs its own 2x capture of that region.
- To show the site as it is, use its screenshots. Rebuilding the page in HTML drifts from the real layout; rebuild only the part that moves, or overlay captured assets at measured positions.
- `--capture-budget` (default 120000 ms) bounds work after navigation; `--timeout` bounds navigation only. Videos are not downloaded: `capture --video <dir> --list`, then `--index N`. `asset-descriptions.md` has vision captions only when `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` is set.
- "very little text content" with an empty asset catalog means the capture is unusable even when it says `ok: true`. A `logo-*.svg` name is a guess from page structure, not proof.
- Brand tokens: link blue `#0000EE` and status reds and greens are never the accent; the accent is the colour that recurs across the most roles. Icon fonts (Font Awesome, icomoon, webflow-icons) are never the display or body face; a captured monospace goes to the mono role. Use only weights the brand font ships, or 600/700 render as fake bold. Every preset has a light ground: for a dark brand, swap ground and ink.
- Capture keeps each `@font-face` rule, `unicode-range` subsets included, in `extracted/page.html`; copying the font files alone loses which characters each covers. Name copied fonts by family, weight and style, or an upright and an italic "Regular" collide.

## From a pull request

- `gh pr view --json files` stops at about 100 files: page `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/N/files`.
- The PR author only opened it: credit commit authors, by commit count (`commits[].authors[]`); skip bots, lockfiles and `dist/`. Reviewers come as logins; names via `gh api users/<login> --jq .name`. TTS reads `@handles` aloud, so speak names.
- Never invent a version. Use the first non-draft release published at or after the merge; else the default branch's `package.json` version as "unreleased"; else only the PR URL.
- Length from size (additions + deletions), as a ceiling: ≲50 lines 20–40 s, 50–200 40–70 s, 200–600 70–110 s, ≳600 lines or 25+ files 110–180 s.
- Show 2–4 hunks of 4–12 lines; counts like +N/−M go on a stat card, not into the voiceover.
- The `code-*` registry blocks (`npx hyperframes catalog --query code --json`) are 1920×1080 scenes driven by `window.__TOKENS` (Shiki tokens, `github-dark`; `fontStyle` bit 1 italic, bit 2 bold) and `window.__BLOCK` (`{id, effect, seq, line?, duration}`). `code-diff` and `code-morph` need at least two states; `code-highlight` counts lines from 0 and `code-scroll` from 1; `code-typing` types at a fixed speed, so check characters × speed against the scene's duration. They reserve no caption band: inset the panel when captions are on.

## On music

- Library music, HeyGen's included, comes as 15–30 s loops: loop the bed to the film with a 0.4 s fade-in and a 1.5 s fade-out. A track whose opening is a quiet build drains a short film: start from a stronger later section.
- Trust beat times only on rhythmic stretches; on calm music the tracker invents a metronome, often at double tempo (`npx hyperframes beats` reports `bpmConfidence`). Cut there on phrase and energy changes; `npx hyperframes audio --only sections,onsets,moments --json` finds them.
- A move that must land on a hit starts 40–190 ms early; a reaction starts 0–45 ms after. The hit itself is a 0 ms `tl.set`: easing a hit kills it. Scenes tile the track with no gaps.
- A word meant to be read holds at least one beat. Any single treatment goes stale after about 6 s: lengthen a section with a hold or a new treatment, never by slowing tweens. On rhythmic sections give footage one clip per strong beat; on calm ones one slow push from 1.0 to 1.08.

## Maps and real places

- A real place (a city, a building, a route, a zoom from the globe to a street) is shown on real imagery. Vector outlines from Natural Earth or GeoJSON read as a diagram and lose the place; keep them for borders and labels drawn on top.
- Live tiles change between renders, so bake the camera move to video with `scripts/bake-basemap.mjs` (MapLibre over Esri satellite or Carto tiles; writes an all-intra MP4 and `<NAME>-coords.json`). From space down to a street: `PROJECTION=globe FROM="lng,lat" CENTER="lng,lat" ZSTART=1.85 ZEND=16` (Earth in a starfield turns from FROM to CENTER, then dives); `--help` lists the rest. It needs network for the tiles and takes well under a second a frame, so bake once, keep the MP4, and run one bake at a time. Draw borders, pins and labels as a live SVG from those coordinates, animating them only while the camera holds.
- Credit the imagery on screen ("Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics" or "© CARTO, © OpenStreetMap") in small type on a soft dark backing, so it holds contrast over bright tiles; mark it `data-layout-ignore` so the type floor in `check` skips it.

## Short motion pieces

- Kinetic type takes 3–7 English words or 4–12 Chinese characters per scene. A count-up runs 1.2–1.6 s, then holds, landing on a downbeat or a hard stop.
- A highlighter that wraps across lines: tween a custom property on a `background-size` band with `box-decoration-break: clone`. `getTotalLength()` can return 0 before layout; give line draw-ons a fallback.
- Hide a round-capped line with a gap longer than the path (`stroke-dasharray="100 120"`, `stroke-dashoffset="110"` on `pathLength="100"`), not dash = gap = offset: that leaves a dot at the end on some curves.
- A point in an image guessed directly misses by 16–24% of the frame. `scripts/locate.mjs` narrows it with a numbered 9×9 grid, then 6×6 on the crop, then a check render (about 2% error).

# The look

Left alone, the same brief comes out with the same look run after run, and banning that look only moves it to the next default. Outside input breaks it, in this order: the project's design spec, a real brand, a reference image or film the person gave you, the subject's own world. Settle it before the first scene, as numbers in the LOOK line (below).

## The project's design spec

Read the first of `frame.md`, `design.md`, `DESIGN.md` at the project root that exists; ignore the rest.

- **Frontmatter is normative**: `colors`, `typography`, `spacing`, `components`. Quote hex values, families and weights exactly; never round or invent them.
- **The prose is intent**: what the look is for, Do's and Don'ts. Follow it for judgment, not values.
- **Brand, not layout**: hex, fonts, weight relationships and Do's and Don'ts are strict; type sizes, spacing, border weight and decoration are yours to scale for video. A 1px border or a 6% shadow from a web page vanishes on screen.

## From a brand

- A website: `npx hyperframes capture <url> --json` writes screenshots, the copy (`extracted/visible-text.txt`), images, logos, `extracted/tokens.json` (colours, fonts) and `extracted/design-styles.json` under its output folder. Look at the screenshots before choosing anything. A capture that exits non-zero, prints `ok: false` or writes `BLOCKED.md` failed: take no brand data from its partial files.
- Figma: `npx hyperframes figma tokens <fileKey>` (`/figma`).
- Images the person attached: take palette and type from what you see.

Use the brand's own fonts when the capture shipped their files or they are bundled (`format.md`); otherwise download the family's `.woff2` into `assets/fonts/` with an `@font-face`, or pick the closest bundled family and say so.

## From a reference

A reference film or image gives its grammar, never its content: shot lengths, how titles enter and leave, the transitions, the palette roles, the type's scale and weight. Snapshot it next to yours (`snapshot --at <t,…> --against ref.mp4`) and write the grammar down, marking what you measured apart from what you guessed.

## The LOOK line

With no design spec, the look is the LOOK line of `SPEC.md` (`spec.md`), taken from the brand, the reference or the subject itself: its era, its materials, where it would be shown. Every part is a number (hex, px, %, a named face and weight), the ground and the hero come from a medium rather than from effects, and the BANNED line keeps it off the defaults. Inter, Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, Geist and JetBrains Mono are where generated design lands; use them when the brand does, not by default. Copy the palette and the faces into the root variables below.

## Video facts

- Full-screen linear gradients on dark grounds band under H.264; use a radial gradient, a solid fill or a solid plus a local glow.
- An accent at 5% opacity disappears in compression: 15–25% for atmosphere, full saturation for the focal element.

## Make it re-brandable

Declare palette and fonts as variables on the root `<html>` and use them everywhere, so the person can re-brand from Studio's Variables panel:

```html
<html
```
